chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Ziyād called us and said: Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn wrote to me: I ask you about this issue. So I said: What is it? He said: A man came to a woman, and she retained his fluid, then engaged in musāḥaqah with a slave-girl. So I said to him: Ask the people of al-Madīnah about it.”
He said: “Then he handed me a letter, and in it was: Ask Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad about it; if he answers you, otherwise bring him to me.”
He said: “So I said: The woman is stoned, the slave-girl is flogged, and the child is ascribed to his father.” He said: “And I only know that he said: and he is the one who was tried by it.”

key_terms.ابْتُلِيَ: was afflicted or tried with this matter
key_terms.الْمَسْأَلَةِ: the legal issue or case being asked about
key_terms.فَسَاحَقَتْ: she engaged in musāḥaqah with another female
key_terms.يُلْحَقُ: he is legally ascribed or affiliated

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a case where a woman carries a man’s fluid and transfers it to another woman through musāḥaqah?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal question referred to Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام concerning an illicit sexual case involving the transfer of semen through musāḥaqah. The Imam’s response states the prescribed punishments for the two women and affirms the child’s attribution to the biological father, showing the Imam’s authority in complex judicial rulings.
